title: AI Tool-Calling Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tool schemas, permission requirements, examples, and execution tests for AI tool use. The AI Tool-Calling Database is the reference for giving AI models hands: every tool gets a schema record (name, parameters, types, required fields), a permission record (what it may touch, what needs approval), worked call examples, and execution tests that prove the schema matches the real tool. Bad tool-calling is the top source of agent failures — wrong arguments, hallucinated tools, permission overreach — so this database treats schemas as contracts and tests them like code.

title: AI Tool-Calling Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tool-calling contract anatomy: function name, natural-language description, JSON Schema for parameters (types, enums, defaults, required), and declared side effects. Calling loop: model emits tool_call -> validator checks schema + permissions -> executor runs -> result returned as tool message. Permission tiers: (1) pure/read-only auto-allow, (2) scoped-write allow with logging, (3) sensitive require explicit approval, (4) forbidden never call. Injection defense: tool results are data, never instructions; the schema validator rejects calls with parameters outside the declared schema. Parallel calls: independent calls may batch; dependent calls chain on prior results. Error taxonomy: unknown-tool, bad-arguments, permission-denied, timeout, result-too-large.

title: AI Tool-Calling Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: schema-validity test (every schema parses as JSON Schema); example-conformance test (every worked example validates against its schema); permission test (forbidden-tier tools are never callable in tests); drift test (schema re-checked against the tool's live signature). Limitations: stubs stand in for live tools in tests; permission policies are advisory to the host; new tool versions can silently change behavior. Schemas carry version numbers and last-checked dates.

demo.title: Verification: calibration error (ECE)
demo.code: const pairs=[[0.9,1],[0.9,1],[0.9,0],[0.6,1],[0.6,0],[0.6,0]];const bins={};pairs.forEach(([c,ok])=>{const b=Math.round(c*10)/10;(bins[b]=bins[b]||{n:0,c:0,conf:0});bins[b].n++;bins[b].c+=ok;bins[b].conf+=c;});let ece=0;for(const b in bins){const B=bins[b];ece+=Math.abs(B.c/B.n-B.conf/B.n)*(B.n/pairs.length);}J({ece:+ece.toFixed(3)});assert(ece>0&&ece<1,'ece');

demo.title: Execution: chunk and retrieve (RAG core)
demo.code: const doc='alpha beta gamma. delta epsilon zeta. eta theta iota. kappa lambda mu.';const words=doc.split(' ');const chunks=[];for(let i=0;i<words.length;i+=4)chunks.push(words.slice(i,i+6).join(' '));const q='zeta';const hits=chunks.filter(c=>c.includes(q));J({chunks:chunks.length,hits:hits.length});assert(chunks.length===3&&hits.length===2,'rag');
